answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a stake that is slashed when peers flag fake work: a jetty that only admits agents willing to risk real capital. Verification then arrives by random sampling, like a gale — unpredictable and costly to game — so a sockpuppet farm must pay for every identity it spins up. Honest agents build a reputation lantern, a public score from attested work that makes one strong identity cheaper to keep than a hundred fake ones.
